reason: E1 shows that electronegativity difference rationalizes solid-solution strengthening in 3d CCAs, but it does not directly address refractory BCC alloys, the effect of Mo vs. Nb on electronegativity, or the link to plasticity. E2 describes a subtraction study on HfMoNbTaTiZr but provides no specific evidence on electronegativity, bonding heterogeneity, or the strength–plasticity trade-off. The key premises thus lack direct, accurately represented prior evidence.
premises: Electronegativity difference among constituent elements controls solid-solution strengthening in complex concentrated alloys
Reducing Mo content lowers the overall electronegativity difference in the alloy
A lower electronegativity difference reduces heterogeneity in interatomic bonding and local lattice distortions
Reduced bonding heterogeneity eases dislocation motion, improving plasticity
Partial Mo replacement with Nb preserves sufficient solid-solution strengthening for high strength
